title: The Ledger of Unspent Days
setting_summary: In the vertical city of Quorum, every resident is issued a finite allotment of counted days, drawn from a central Ledger and enforced by turnstiles, ration clocks, and roaming auditors. When the Ledger begins silently reclaiming days from citizens who have committed no offense, a small records office becomes the only place where the arithmetic can be challenged. The city's hierarchy runs on scarcity and surveillance, so any demand for dignity, voice, or equality must first be argued as a correction to the count itself.
